item.title: Financial Inclusion Officer - Senegal
item.description:
Location: Dakar, Sine Saloum or Casamance, with signiﬁcant national travel

Contract type and duration: Two years (with the possibility of extension thereafter)

Hours: Full-time

Closing date for applications: 3 November 2026

Reports to: Head of Technical Capacity for West Africa

Start date: 1 December 2026

Remuneration: Circa XOF 8,988,369 - 10,691,433 gross annually

We unlock power with coastal communities

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

Summary job description

The Financial Inclusion Officer will support the delivery of Blue Ventures’ Financial Inclusion programme in Senegal and The Gambia, working closely with partners and coastal communities to strengthen financial resilience and improve household livelihoods. The role involves developing, adapting, and implementing practical tools, guidelines, training materials, and approaches related to financial literacy, VSLA management, savings and loans, business development, and income-generating activities.

The Officer will also provide technical support, training, mentoring, and peer-learning opportunities to partners and communities, contribute to knowledge development and sharing of good practices, support data collection and analysis, and help integrate financial inclusion and sustainable livelihood approaches into broader fisheries management and conservation programmes. The position requires frequent travel, and involves collaboration with local partners, communities, and Blue Ventures’ international teams. Reporting to the West Africa Head of Technical Capacity, this is a full-time role based in Senegal.

item.title: Partnership Coordinator - Senegal
item.description:
Location: Senegal - with frequent travel requirements

Contract type and duration: Two-year fixed-term contract, with a possibility of extension

Hours: Full-time

Closing date for applications: 2 November 2026

Reports to: Head of Partnership Network West Africa

Start date: As soon as possible

Remuneration: Circa XOF 11,864,647 - 17,559,677 gross per annum

We unlock power with coastal communities

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

Summary job description

Blue Ventures’ Partner Network team is responsible for identifying, selecting, and supporting civil society organisations and NGOs that work with coastal communities around the world. The team provides funding, technical assistance, and organisational support to help partners develop and sustain community-based fisheries management and locally managed marine areas. The team also promotes collaboration, knowledge sharing, and capacity building among partners, helping them strengthen their organisations and contribute to a global network focused on sustainable coastal fisheries management, with local communities at the centre of decision-making.

Blue Ventures is recruiting a Partnership Coordinator in Senegal to help expand and strengthen its partner network. The main responsibilities include developing partnership strategies, identifying potential partners, assessing their needs, building and maintaining relationships, fostering collaboration, and supporting successful partnership initiatives. The position is full-time, based in Senegal, and reports to the Head of Partnership for West Africa. The role requires frequent travel to remote communities, flexibility to accommodate weather- and tide-dependent schedules, and the ability to work effectively across multiple time zones.

item.title: Partner-Centred Design Consultant
item.description:
Location: Global

Closing date for applications: Monday, 26 October 2026

Start date: As soon as Possible

Consultancy duration: Three to Four Months

Consultancy budget: Circa GBP 25,000 gross

We unlock power with coastal communities

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities, restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

Summary job description

We seek a consultant or team with strong experience in service design, customer experience (CX), user experience (UX) or human-centred service transformation to bring an independent partner-experience perspective and organisational critique to this work.

The consultancy will examine the end-to-end experience of working with Blue Ventures and connect it to the organisational choices shaping that experience. This includes how functions such as training and learning, partnerships, programme performance, data science and advocacy engage partners and coordinate their work.

Direct partner research will inform the assignment. The consultant must also bring the expertise to interpret and challenge existing arrangements, develop alternative approaches and demonstrate how support could be designed and delivered differently.

The work should introduce a shared framework that Blue Ventures can continue using beyond the consultancy. By applying this framework to selected priority areas, the consultant should demonstrate its value and help teams develop the understanding and practices needed to maintain it. The assignment is not expected to identify or design every change the organisation may need.

The primary focus will be partners funded through the Frontline Community Fund (FCF) and their interactions across Blue Ventures. The consultancy will complement our wider Partnership Strategy and internal operating model review, informing both without taking responsibility for the overall strategy, a comprehensive internal efficiency review or full implementation of recommendations.

item.title: Senior Marine Ecology Officer - Southeast Asia
item.description:
Location: Bali, Indonesia

Closing date for applications: November 1st, 2026

Start date: As soon as possible

Contract duration: Permanent

Remuneration: IDR 255,498,264 to IDR 305,344,256 per Annum

We rebuild tropical fisheries with coastal communities

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

Summary job description

We are currently recruiting a Senior Marine Ecology Officer - Southeast Asia, technical support to Blue Ventures’ marine ecology operations across Southeast Asia. Reporting directly to the Data Science Manager - Asia and based full-time in Denpasar, Indonesia (with regular regional travel), the role will support community-based ecology monitoring, management, and governance, working closely with teams in Indonesia, Timor-Leste, and the Philippines as well as regional partners across Southeast Asia. Working closely with the global Spatial Ecology team, you will execute the technical development, workflow standardization, field-level rollout of mobile data technologies, and tailored learning resources that bridge science and community-led conservation.

The Senior Officer will be in charge of capacity-building initiatives—including hands-on workshops, technical mentoring, and peer exchanges—to translate ecological theory into practical, community-level action. We are seeking a dynamic technical person with proven expertise in mangrove, seagrass and coral reef, participatory monitoring, and ecosystem-based fisheries governance in Southeast Asia. You will bring a strong track record in community-led natural resource management, multi-stakeholder partnership building, and optional familiarity with coastal carbon markets. If you thrive in complex environments, work independently across disciplines, and share our commitment to human rights-based marine conservation, this role offers an exciting opportunity to drive regional impact.
